# System requirements {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 4 &middot; PART B]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

[OS libraries that R packages need to build and load.]{.subhead}

## `SystemRequirements`

In the shell of the block 4 container, after `q()`:

```bash
R -q -e 'download.packages("xml2", destdir = ".")'

tar xzf xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz
grep -A1 SystemRequirements xml2/DESCRIPTION
```

```text
SystemRequirements: libxml2: libxml2-dev (deb), libxml2-devel (rpm)
Collate: 'S4.R' 'as_list.R' 'xml_parse.R' 'as_xml_document.R'
```

The same field in a few other CRAN packages:

```text
sf:        GDAL (>= 2.0.1), GEOS (>= 3.4.0), PROJ (>= 4.8.0), sqlite3
rjags:     JAGS 4.x.y
RPostgres: libpq >= 9.0: libpq-dev (deb) or postgresql-devel (rpm)
V8:        On Linux you can build against libv8-dev (Debian) or v8-devel (Fedora). ...
curl:      libcurl (>= 7.73): libcurl-devel (rpm) or libcurl4-openssl-dev (deb)
```

## The field is free text

- **No required format.** Every maintainer writes it differently
  ([r-system-requirements](https://github.com/rstudio/r-system-requirements)).
- **Not in CRAN's `PACKAGES`.** CRAN's index has no `SystemRequirements`
  field, so `install.packages()` never sees it. Package Manager's index
  does include it.

`install.packages()` cannot warn you, check beforehand, or install OS
packages. It compiles, fails, and shows you the compiler output.

## Reading the error

The `ANTICONF ERROR` block names what is missing and the Debian package to
install:

```text
Configuration failed because libxml-2.0 was not found. Try installing:
 * deb: libxml2-dev (Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine, etc)
```

`xml2`'s own `configure` script prints this
([configure](https://github.com/r-lib/xml2/blob/main/configure)). Without
such a hint, read the last lines before `ERROR:`.

## Failure phase → fix {.skip}

```text
configure: ... was not found              -> missing -dev package (headers)
foo.c:12:10: fatal error: x.h             -> missing -dev package (headers)
ld: cannot find -lfoo                     -> missing -dev package (library)
unable to load shared object '.../foo.so'
  libfoo.so.1: cannot open shared object  -> missing runtime library
```

::: {.note}
[Installs, then fails to load]{.note-label}
The headers were there at build time; the shared library is not there at
run time. Run `ldd <pkg>/libs/<pkg>.so` and look for `not found`.
:::

## Fixing it

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

After `q()`:

```bash
apt-get update && apt-get install -y libxml2-dev
```

```bash
# confirm what we got
dpkg -L libxml2-dev | grep 'tree\.h'
xml2-config --cflags
pkg-config --modversion libxml-2.0
```

```text
/usr/include/libxml2/libxml/tree.h
-I/usr/include/libxml2
2.15.4
```

Retry, and it compiles:

```r
install.packages("xml2")
library(xml2)
read_xml("<a><b>hi</b></a>")
```

## `r-system-requirements`

Posit maintains rules that map the free text to OS packages, per
distribution
([rstudio/r-system-requirements](https://github.com/rstudio/r-system-requirements)).
Package Manager and `pak` use them.

Each rule is a regular expression over `SystemRequirements`, and the OS
packages to install per distribution:

```json
{
  "patterns": ["\\blibxml2\\b"],
  "dependencies": [{
    "packages": ["libxml2-dev"],
    "constraints": [{ "os": "linux", "distribution": "debian" }]
  }]
}
```

Supported distributions include Debian 13 and unstable, Ubuntu 22.04 to
26.04, and RHEL 7 to 10 (see the README for the full list).

## Package Manager sysreqs API

An HTTP API, so it works from a Dockerfile or shell script without R.

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
curl -s "https://packagemanager.posit.co/__api__/repos/cran/sysreqs\
?all=false&pkgname=xml2&distribution=debian&release=13"
```

```json
{"requirements":[{"name":"xml2","requirements":{
  "packages":["libxml2-dev"],
  "install_scripts":["apt-get install -y libxml2-dev"]}}]}
```


## `pak::pkg_sysreqs()`

```r
install.packages("pak", repos = sprintf(
  "https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/%s/%s/%s",
  .Platform$pkgType, R.Version()$os, R.Version()$arch))
pak::pkg_sysreqs("xml2", sysreqs_platform = "debian-13")
```

```text
-- Install scripts -----------------------------------------
apt-get -y update
apt-get -y install libxml2-dev

-- Packages and their system dependencies ------------------
xml2  - libxml2-dev
```


## Sysreqs for a package set

`pkg_sysreqs()` resolves the dependency tree first, so you get the system
requirements of the whole set
([`?pak::pkg_sysreqs`](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/pkg_sysreqs.html)).

```r
pak::pkg_sysreqs(c("sf", "RPostgres", "xml2"),
                 sysreqs_platform = "debian-13")
```

In a Dockerfile, with `pak` installed. `install_scripts` alone leaves out
`pre_install`, which holds `apt-get update`:

```dockerfile
RUN Rscript -e 's <- pak::pkg_sysreqs("sf", sysreqs_platform = "debian-13"); \
      writeLines(c(s$pre_install, s$install_scripts, s$post_install), \
                 "/tmp/sysreqs.sh")' \
 && sh -e /tmp/sysreqs.sh && rm /tmp/sysreqs.sh
```

When `pak` does the installing, it installs the OS packages itself if R
runs as root or with password-less `sudo`
([pak system requirements](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/sysreqs.html)):

```r
pak::pkg_install("sf")
```

## When the mapping is wrong or absent

1. **Read the field.** In the tarball's `DESCRIPTION`, or with
   `tools::CRAN_package_db()`.
2. **Read `configure`.** In an Anticonf script, `PKG_CONFIG_NAME`,
   `PKG_DEB_NAME` and `PKG_TEST_HEADER` say what it looks for
   ([xml2's configure](https://github.com/r-lib/xml2/blob/main/configure)).
3. **Search by file.** `apt-file search libxml/tree.h` finds the package
   that provides a header (install it first with
   `apt-get install -y apt-file && apt-file update`); on RHEL,
   `dnf provides '*/libxml/tree.h'`.

Missing rules can be contributed to `r-system-requirements`.
